newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares close higher, EDP weakens.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares close higher, EDP weakens.

text.p: 1615 GMT - Portuguese shares ended higher, but utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal bucked the overall trend of the market and ended weaker following a Merrill Lynch "reduce" recommendation. Merrill Lynch recommended clients reduce their holdings in EDP, saying that the company was "sound but overvalued." "Our initial opinion is reduce, with an expectation that the shares will move below our 12-month price objective of 3,000 escudos," the investment house said in a client advisory, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters.
* Lisbon bourse was buoyed by rising foreign markets after Wall Street rebounded from last Friday's plunge.

* The market waited to see whether the Federal Open Market Committee, the policy arm of the Federal Reserve, would raise U.S. rates. Most analysts polled by Reuters did not expect the Fed to raise rates. A decision on rates is expected to be announced after 1800 GMT.

* Dealers said they expected the Lisbon market to edge higher tomorrow. "I think that tomorrow the market could rise again, because the Fed is not expected to raise rates. The Portuguese market is still in good shape, interest rates are falling, and companies have shown good results and will continue to do so," said one dealer.
* Turnover in the cash market was 14 billion escudos.
* PSI20 .PSI20 index of 20 leading stocks up 71.09 points to 8,225.03
